_doc: WORKED EXAMPLE of the v3 DETAIL BIBLE (format: briefs/v3/BIBLE_TEMPLATE.json). Story: SCRIPT_REPORT 5.6 Script 1, as linted in briefs/v3/award/SCRIPT.md (PASS). Times are the linter's estimates (est_t0) until the voice is locked.
title: The Award That Made Kids Miss School

characters.speaker: MOM
characters.voice: cast 3 warm adult female candidates, 4+ takes, pick by clarity + timbre distance from James

look.notes: warm and bright everywhere, even February: overcastWarm, never grey-blue; mean chroma ~24; ink only on the cards; story colours = the three envelopes (grey / blue / yellow) and the gold certificate

cast.role: YOU: the perfect-attendance kid (about 10), the hero
Mom, proud, the doubter (she is SURE it works)
the researcher in the mail room (generic, never a likeness)
cast.signature: grey vest + rubber stamp + pencil behind the ear

sets.place: a warm family kitchen, early morning, sun through the window over the sink

ground.meso: tile joints with depth, slight bevel

props.where: back wall, right of the window

practicals.what: pendant lamp over the table (warm, off at the start, on in s17)

sets.ambience: kitchen morning: fridge hum, distant birds outside, a clock tick

sets.place: the front hall in January: a door with a brass letterbox, a doormat, wet boots, snow outside the door glass
sets.ambience: hall: muffled street outside, a radiator tick

sets.place: a tree-lined street to school in autumn, low gold sun, leaves falling
sets.ambience: street autumn: wind in leaves, distant traffic, kids far off

sets.place: a school-district mail room: a long sorting table, thousands of envelopes in three colours

props.where: on the table: grey / blue / yellow
table end: NO LETTER / PROMISE / CERTIFICATE

practicals.what: two long ceiling lamps (warm-white, not green fluorescent)
desk lamp at the stamping station

sets.ambience: mail room: paper shuffles, a desk fan, a franking thunk now and then

sets.place: a cosy school staff room: mugs, a coffee machine, a whiteboard, about 20 teachers

ground.meso: carpet pile normal + a worn path

sets.ambience: staff room: murmur, a spoon on a mug, the coffee machine gurgle

sets.place: the school gate on a February morning: frost, puddles, kids arriving, a big calendar board

surfaces.meso: window insets, sills, a roof edge

vegetation.where: bare winter branches behind the wall

sets.ambience: school gate: kids chatter, a distant bus, crows

sets.place: a sunny classroom: rows of desks, a big wall calendar, a chalkboard, morning shafts through tall windows

surfaces.meso: window insets with deep sills, skirting

props.where: side wall: FEBRUARY, rows grey / blue / yellow

practicals.what: ceiling lamps (on, dim against the sun shafts)

sets.ambience: classroom: chairs, pencils, a clock tick, muffled playground

sets.place: the kid's bedroom at dawn: blinds throwing bars of light, the alarm clock, posters

surfaces.meso: window frame + blinds slats with depth

practicals.what: bedside lamp (off; a warm glow only in s19 if needed)

sets.ambience: bedroom dawn: birds outside, soft heating hum

shots.line: Schools mailed kids an award for a perfect month of school.

framings.desc: FRAME 0 = thumbnail: the fridge door with the gold certificate under a magnet, the alarm clock on the counter beside it, morning shaft from the window
framings.subject: certificate

framings.desc: the push ends close on the certificate: PERFECT ATTENDANCE readable, the clock edge in frame
framings.subject: certificate

light.notes: a warm sun shaft across the fridge door; dust motes in it

surfaces_near.where: counter edge in the lower frame

vegetation.where: window sill, out of focus left

life.what: dust motes drifting in the sun shaft
steam curling from the kettle spout
a fridge magnet letter swings after the fridge hum shudder
the alarm clock's second hand ticks

shots.line: The next month, they missed more.
shots.location: the back of the class, the empty desk

framings.desc: a row of full desks, one EMPTY desk in the middle; behind it the wall calendar with red gaps
framings.subject: desks

light.notes: shafts through the tall windows across the desks

life.what: kids at the full desks fidget, one yawns
dust motes in the window shafts
a paper corner on the notice board lifts in the draught

acting.action: a kid glances at the empty chair, shrugs

shots.line: Imagine you're one of them.

framings.desc: the kid walks toward the lens, beanie and yellow backpack, leaves falling, gold back-light
framings.subject: kid

light.notes: dapple from the crowns slides over the kid; warm rim

life.what: leaves falling and blowing across the path
a cyclist crosses far behind
crowns sway in the wind (shadows move)
two birds hop and flutter off as the kid passes

acting.action: walks with a bounce, hitches the backpack strap

shots.line: Last autumn, you went a whole month without missing a day.
shots.location: along the street to the school fence

framings.desc: side-on: the kid walks right to left past the houses, the light stepping from gold to noon to gold (days passing)
framings.subject: kid

framings.desc: the kid reaches the school fence; the tally board 'DAYS: 20 / 20' gets its last tick
framings.subject: tally_board

light.notes: a fast sun sweep on the house fronts = days passing (rig_opts animated by the set)

life.what: a dog on a lead sniffs a lamp post
leaves blowing
a car passes on the road behind
other kids join the walk in the second framing

acting.action: skips the last two steps, taps the fence

shots.line: Then, in January, an envelope arrives with your name on it.

framings.desc: floor level: the letterbox flap snaps open, a yellow envelope drops toward the lens onto the mat; snow falling outside the door glass
framings.subject: front_door

framings.desc: the kid's hand picks it up; the envelope reads the kid's name (a board on the envelope)
framings.subject: kid

light.notes: cold daylight through the door glass vs the warm hall lamp

life.what: snow falling beyond the door glass
the letterbox flap swings and settles
melt water drips off a boot

fx.what: a puff of grit when the envelope lands

acting.action: crouches, picks the envelope up, eyes widen at the name

shots.line: Inside: a certificate. "Perfect Attendance."

framings.desc: top-down over the table: the kid's hands tear the envelope, the gold certificate slides out between the fruit bowl and a cereal box
framings.subject: certificate

light.notes: window light from the top of frame, crisp shadows of the hands

life.what: cereal flakes scatter as the envelope is pulled
steam from a mug at the frame edge
a cat paw reaches for the envelope corner

fx.what: a tiny gold glint sweeps the certificate seal

acting.action: tears the envelope, slides the certificate out

shots.line: Your mom sticks it on the fridge: "Now you'll never miss a day!" (MOM)

framings.desc: mom slaps the certificate on the fridge with a magnet, the kid beside her
framings.subject: mom

framings.desc: the orbit ends on mom's proud face and wagging finger on her line, the kid grinning below
framings.subject: mom

light.notes: window light on mom's face, warm rim; the clock on the counter stays in frame (plant)

life.what: steam from mom's mug
the magnet letters on the fridge rattle from the slap
the curtain moves in a draught

acting.action: slaps the certificate on with a magnet (wind-up 5 f, slap, overshoot)
wags a finger, says her line (talk cycle on her words)
nods hard, beams

shots.line: But it isn't just a nice surprise. It's a test.

framings.desc: close: a yellow envelope under the desk lamp; the clerk's hand stamps it
framings.subject: envelope_piles

framings.desc: the pull-back reveals the long table: thousands of envelopes; on 'test' the clerk lifts a sly eyebrow
framings.subject: clerk

light.notes: a pool of warm desk-lamp light in a dimmer room: the reveal walks out of the pool

life.what: the desk fan turns, papers lift at the table end
a second worker wheels a trolley of envelopes across the back
dust motes in the lamp beam

acting.action: stamps the envelope (a firm thunk)
looks up at the lens, one eyebrow up

shots.line: More than 15,000 students were split into three groups.

framings.desc: high top-down: three rivers of envelopes (grey / blue / yellow) flowing into three trays; the whiteboard '15,000 STUDENTS' at the edge
framings.subject: envelope_piles

framings.desc: the rise ends wide and high: the whole table, three trays filling, workers as small figures
framings.subject: sort_table

light.notes: even warm top light; the three colours lead

life.what: envelopes slide in three streams (instanced, staggered)
three workers sort with quick hands
the desk fan turns

acting.action: pushes the last stack into the third tray

shots.line: One group got nothing.

framings.desc: the grey tray labelled NO LETTER: the clerk drops it into a bin with a shrug; dust puffs
framings.subject: trays

life.what: dust puff from the bin
a worker behind carries a crate
the fan-blown paper flutters on the table

acting.action: tips the empty grey tray into a bin, shrugs

sound.event: hollow tray tip into a bin

shots.line: One got a promise: "Be perfect in February, and you could win an award."

framings.desc: macro over a blue letter being folded: 'BE PERFECT IN FEBRUARY' readable
framings.subject: envelope_piles

framings.desc: push past the letter to the clerk sliding it into a blue envelope, a blue trophy doodle on the board behind
framings.subject: clerk

life.what: paper edges flutter in the fan draught
a worker behind stacks blue envelopes
the desk lamp beam with motes

acting.action: folds the letter in thirds, slides it into a blue envelope

sound.event: paper fold + slide into the envelope

shots.line: And one got the surprise certificate. Like you.

framings.desc: the yellow pile glows under the lamp; the clerk lifts ONE yellow envelope to the lens: 'TO: YOU'
framings.subject: envelope_piles

framings.desc: on 'Like you.' the envelope fills the frame: TO: YOU, the clerk's wink behind it
framings.subject: envelope_piles

light.notes: the yellow envelope catches the lamp: the gold of the story

life.what: the stack settles and one envelope slides off
dust motes in the lamp
a worker passes behind out of focus

acting.action: holds the envelope up to the lens, a wink

shots.line: Ask teachers what happens next. Only 2 in 100 say it will backfire.

framings.desc: over a teacher's shoulder to the whiteboard 'WILL IT BACKFIRE?'; teachers chatting with mugs
framings.subject: whiteboard

framings.desc: the pull-back finds TWO raised hands among about twenty teachers who laugh it off
framings.subject: teachers

light.notes: warm lamps + a window strip; the two raised hands catch a sun patch

life.what: steam from the coffee machine and mugs
teachers sip, nudge, chuckle (crowd idles)
the window blind sways

acting.action: two hands go up; the rest wave it off with a laugh

sound.event: staff room murmur + spoon on mug

shots.line: So, February. Who shows up?

framings.desc: the calendar board flips to FEBRUARY; the crane drops to the gate where kids in coats stream in, frost on the pavers
framings.subject: calendar_board

light.notes: soft warm overcast, puddle reflections; still bright (owner: warm, never grey)

surfaces_near.where: the ground in front of the gate

life.what: kids stream through the gate with breath puffs
crows lift off the wall
a bus passes beyond the fence
puddle ripples from footsteps

acting.action: kids hurry in, one checks a watch

sound.event: kids chatter + footsteps on wet pavers

shots.line: The promise? It changed nothing.

framings.desc: the promise kid (blue puffer) drops into his seat on time as always; behind him the calendar's BLUE row: steady ticks
framings.subject: promise_kid

light.notes: window shafts; the blue row in sun

life.what: classmates unpack bags
dust motes in the shafts
the wall clock's second hand

acting.action: plops down, a small shrug to camera

shots.line: The certificate? Those kids had about 8% more absences than kids who got nothing.
shots.location: the wall calendar + the empty desk

framings.desc: the YELLOW row of the calendar: ticks, then gaps popping in (red)
framings.subject: wall_calendar

framings.desc: the camera slides to the empty desk with a yellow backpack hook bare; board '+8% ABSENCES' on the calendar edge
framings.subject: desks

light.notes: a sun patch slides off the empty chair (time passing)

life.what: gaps pop in on the yellow row one by one
kids at the other desks work, one passes a note
dust motes in the sun patch

acting.action: the kid next to the empty desk glances at it

shots.line: You see, the award didn't just say "well done."

framings.desc: the certificate on the fridge, the pendant lamp now on (evening), the orbit catches the gold seal
framings.subject: certificate

framings.desc: the orbit ends with the pendant lamp's warm pool and the dark window: evening has come
framings.subject: certificate

light.notes: dusk through the window + the warm pendant pool

life.what: the pendant lamp sways slightly
steam from a pot on the hob
mom passes behind, out of focus, humming

fx.what: a slow gold glint across the seal

shots.line: It probably also said: "you're ahead of the other kids."

framings.desc: a chalk bar chart: the kid's bar towers with a gold star, the others small
framings.subject: chalkboard

framings.desc: the push lands on the kid at the board, arms folded, smug, chin up
framings.subject: kid

light.notes: a sun shaft on the kid like a spotlight (comic)

life.what: chalk dust drifting off the board
classmates roll their eyes and whisper
a paper plane glides across the back

acting.action: folds arms, lifts the chin, a slow smug nod

shots.line: And when you're already ahead... one lazy morning feels earned.

framings.desc: high over the bed: the kid curled in the duvet, blind bars of dawn light crossing the face
framings.subject: kid

framings.desc: the crane settles beside the pillow: the kid opens one eye at the alarm clock, smiles, burrows
framings.subject: kid

light.notes: low dawn sun through the blinds: bars of light across the card (the LOOK_REPORT's strongest card-in-light trick)

life.what: the blinds sway, the light bars slide
a cat stretches at the foot of the bed
dust motes in the light bars
birds outside the window

acting.action: one eye opens, a sly smile, burrows back under

shots.line: The certificate stays on the fridge...

framings.desc: the certificate on the fridge, quiet morning; the counter alarm clock reads 7:00
framings.subject: certificate

light.notes: same as s01 (the callback)

life.what: dust motes in the shaft
kettle steam
the clock's second hand

shots.line: ...while you hit snooze.

framings.desc: the alarm clock ringing on the bedside table; a hand slaps the snooze button on the word
framings.subject: alarm_clock_bed

light.notes: blind bars on the table and the hand

life.what: the clock's bells shake
dust motes in the light bars
the blinds sway

acting.action: a hand flops out of the duvet and slaps the snooze (squash on impact)

shots.line: (tail: the loop)

framings.desc: back on the fridge: the camera eases into EXACTLY frame 0's pose; the last frame = frame 0
framings.subject: certificate

light.notes: identical to s01 at frame 0

life.what: dust motes (whole cycles over the film: loop rule)
kettle steam
the clock's second hand

music.mood: warm, curious, a little cheeky (pizzicato + celesta + soft brushes), no circus

changes.what: a hush: only a ticking motif
a small swell into the reveal
stop dead on the slap; the ambience carries the tail

music.end: stops on the last word; only the ambience runs through the loop tail

loop.frame0: s01: the certificate on the fridge, the alarm clock beside it, the morning shaft
loop.last: s22 eases into s01's start pose; periodic life on whole cycles; frame TOTAL == frame 0 (pixel check)
